core.title: Declare every initial flow variables input on the user/system flow
core.given: A user/system flow definition for which any artifact may be seeded into flow variables before the first product capability step, whether or not a product capability reads it.
core.when: The planner authors or edits the user/system flow.
core.then: Declare every artifact flow variables may be seeded with under inputs.caller (caller-provided) or inputs.spec_materialized (deterministically materialized from the spec).
prefer: Classify each initial artifact explicitly: caller-provided goes in inputs.caller; anything derived deterministically from the spec goes in inputs.spec_materialized.
Mark which initial inputs are required so missing ones can be rejected before step 1.
avoid: Relying on an undeclared artifact being present in flow variables at user/system flow start; undeclared initial inputs are rejected before step 1.
Leaving a required initial input unsupplied or unmaterialized; missing required initial inputs are rejected before step 1.
Placing non-deterministic or caller-supplied data under inputs.spec_materialized.
core.why: Flow variables is seeded and validated before the first product capability step, so the journey can only start from declared initial inputs; undeclared inputs or missing required initial inputs must fail fast before step 1 rather than mid-sequence.
evidence: The user/system flow definition contains inputs.caller and/or inputs.spec_materialized listing every artifact seeded into flow variables.
Every artifact that may be seeded into flow variables before step 1 appears in inputs.caller or inputs.spec_materialized.
Running the user/system flow with an undeclared initial input or a missing required initial input is rejected before step 1.
verification: Declared initial inputs are the user/system flow's inputs.caller and inputs.spec_materialized blocks; these are seeded into flow variables and validated before the first product capability step.

Reject before step 1 when flow variables is seeded with an artifact not declared in inputs.caller or inputs.spec_materialized, or when a required declared initial input is missing; absent optional inputs are not grounds for rejection.
Until an automated validator is bound to this rule, compliance is established by review of the user/system flow definition.

values: set of artifacts seeded into flow variables before step 1 changed

fires: Planner authors a new user/system flow for which any artifact may be seeded into flow variables (caller-provided or materialized from the spec), including seeded artifacts that no product capability reads.
Planner edits a user/system flow so that the set of artifacts that may be seeded into flow variables before step 1 changes.
Planner adds or removes entries under the user/system flow's inputs.caller or inputs.spec_materialized.
doesNotFire: Planner edits a product capability's internal acceptances without changing which artifacts may be seeded into flow variables.
Documentation or planning work that does not touch a user/system flow definition.
Artifacts produced by an earlier product capability step within the user/system flow (those are not initial inputs).

neutralityNotes: The convention is planner-model-level rather than stack-level: user/system flow, product capability step, journey, flow variables (the working store seeded before the first product capability step) and the user/system flow schema blocks inputs.caller / inputs.spec_materialized are cross-stack ATDD planner vocabulary (user-system-flow/capability/journey are artifacts in the closed urn group, and notProfileKeys permits task terms in neutral core activation), so the core keeps them verbatim for fidelity rather than routing them through the profile. The only stack datum needed is the concrete plan-artifact kind of a user/system flow definition (roles.plan_artifact.kinds); bun.json names no path, suffix, runner or tooling for user/system flow definitions, so no other profile key is required and none is proposed. The activation facts' explanatory notes (user/system-flow-definition file, diff-level observer) are realization guidance captured by the facts' values and observability. The D2 (#1086) validator binding is the sole realization-only content (bunOnly); until a validator is bound, the core keeps the neutral review-based compliance path.
